name: F-2-7 Points-Based Long-Term Resident

requirement_groups.name: Points-based assessment for E- or D-visa holders

requirements.blocker_text: Open only to foreigners currently on an E-series (employment) or D-series (study, trade, investment) visa; it is a status change, not a first-entry visa.
requirements.fix_path: Hold a qualifying E- or D-series visa before applying.

requirements.blocker_text: Requires 80 or more points on a scored assessment combining age, education, Korean-language ability (TOPIK), income, time already spent in Korea, social integration (KIIP participation), and special achievements or awards.
requirements.fix_path: Improve individual point categories -- KIIP completion, TOPIK level, or documented income increases are the most commonly used levers.

evidence_required.document: Points-assessment application with supporting documentation for each scored category
TOPIK certificate or KIIP completion record

sources.title: HiKorea -- Korea Immigration Service's official portal for visa categories, ARC, and stay procedures
Living in Korea -- Korean Visa Types Explained, corroborating the 80+ point threshold and scored categories for F-2-7

notes: STRUCTURAL FINDING: F-2-7 is the single most consequential intermediate status in Korea's entire route graph -- it is the fastest documented path to F-5 permanent residence in this dataset (F-5-16: 3 years on F-2-7 plus only 1x GNI income, versus the general F-5-1 track's 5 years plus 2x GNI), which is why pr_after_months and citizenship_after_months here (36) are meaningfully faster than kr_e7_designated_activities' or kr_d8_corporate_investment's own top-level defaults (60), even though F-2-7 itself typically requires holding an E- or D-visa first. A real, documented adversarial case worth flagging: one sourced example (allvisakorea.com) describes an applicant who spent 18 years in Korea on E-9 to E-7-4 to F-2-7 to reach F-5, specifically because the F-2-7 points system's scoring criteria for education and income changed materially between when they first applied (2017) and later years -- illustrating that points thresholds and scoring weights are not static, unlike most other hard-requirement figures in this dataset which are simple salary floors. A key practical advantage over most other Korea work routes: F-2-7 holders can bring accompanying family members with the same application (not modeled as a separate outcome field, but worth surfacing on the route detail page), a benefit not shared by e.g. kr_e9_eps_nonprofessional's flat family exclusion. F-2-7 grants full employment freedom without requiring a specific employer sponsor, a structural difference from the E-7 track's employer-tied status -- functionally the closest Korea equivalent to the UK's Global Talent or Portugal's D7-style unsponsored long-term routes documented elsewhere in this dataset.
